text: Protons give an atom its identity, electrons its personality.
author: Bill Bryson
source: A Short History of Nearly Everything (2003)

text: A mathematician will recognize Cauchy, Gauss, Jacobi, or Helmholtz after reading a few pages, just as musicians recognize from the first few bars Mozart, Beethoven, or Schubert.
author: Ludwig Boltzmann
source: Quoted in Arthur Koestler, The Act of Creation (1964) (often cited as p. 265)

text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan Turing

text: All models are wrong, but some are useful.
author: George E. P. Box
source: Robustness in the strategy of scientific model building (1979) / widely attributed to Box

text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself—and you are the easiest person to fool.
author: Richard P. Feynman

text: Science is what we have learned about how to keep from fooling ourselves.
author: Richard P. Feynman

text: A new scientific truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents but rather because its opponents eventually die.
author: Max Planck

text: What we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning.
author: Werner Heisenberg

text: Science is built up with facts, as a house is with stones; but a collection of facts is no more a science than a heap of stones is a house.
author: Henri Poincaré

text: The most incomprehensible thing about the world is that it is comprehensible.
author: Albert Einstein

text: God does not play dice with the universe.
author: Albert Einstein

text: If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of Giants.
author: Isaac Newton

text: Nature is pleased with simplicity.
author: Isaac Newton
source: Principia / commonly attributed to Newton (exact phrasing varies)

text: In questions of science, the authority of a thousand is not worth the humble reasoning of a single individual.
author: Galileo Galilei
source: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems (1632) (attribution/translation varies)

text: Mathematics is the language in which God has written the universe.
author: Galileo Galilei

text: If you can't explain it simply, you don't understand it well enough.
author: Albert Einstein

text: Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
author: Carl Sagan

text: Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
author: Carl Sagan

text: The good thing about science is that it’s true whether or not you believe in it.
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

text: The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers.
author: Richard W. Hamming
source: Numerical Methods for Scientists and Engineers (1962) / widely attributed to Hamming

text: When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it.
author: William Thomson (Lord Kelvin)
source: Popular Lectures and Addresses (1883) / widely cited

text: The great tragedy of science—the slaying of a beautiful hypothesis by an ugly fact.
author: Thomas H. Huxley

text: The universe is under no obligation to make sense to you.
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson

text: Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known.
author: Carl Sagan

text: Science is the belief in the ignorance of experts.
author: Richard P. Feynman
source: The Meaning of It All (1998) / phrasing varies in transcripts

text: A theory can be proved by experiment; but no path leads from experiment to the birth of a theory.
author: Albert Einstein

text: The scientist is not a person who gives the right answers, but one who asks the right questions.
author: Claude Lévi-Strauss

text: Science may be described as the art of systematic over-simplification.
author: Karl Popper
source: The Open Society and Its Enemies / attribution varies

text: Our knowledge can only be finite, while our ignorance must necessarily be infinite.
author: Karl Popper

text: Normal science does not aim at novelties of fact or theory and, when successful, finds none.
author: Thomas S. Kuhn

text: The greatest enemy of knowledge is not ignorance, it is the illusion of knowledge.
author: Stephen Hawking

text: If you wish to make an apple pie from scratch, you must first invent the universe.
author: Carl Sagan

text: The whole of science is nothing more than a refinement of everyday thinking.
author: Albert Einstein

text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
author: Charles Darwin

text: We are to admit no more causes of natural things than such as are both true and sufficient to explain their appearances.
author: Isaac Newton

text: The aim of science is not to open the door to infinite wisdom, but to set a limit to infinite error.
author: Bertolt Brecht
source: The Life of Galileo (1938) (quote often attributed to Brecht)

text: It is the tension between creativity and skepticism that has produced the stunning and unexpected findings of science.
author: Carl Sagan

text: The test of all knowledge is experiment. Experiment is the sole judge of scientific truth.
author: Richard P. Feynman
source: The Feynman Lectures on Physics (Vol. I)

text: An expert is a person who has made all the mistakes that can be made in a very narrow field.
author: Niels Bohr

text: How wonderful that we have met with a paradox. Now we have some hope of making progress.
author: Niels Bohr

text: The laws of physics and chemistry are completely known, and the difficulty is only that the exact application leads to equations too complex to be soluble.
author: P. A. M. Dirac

text: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existing.
author: Albert Einstein

text: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
author: Richard P. Feynman
source: Commonly attributed (seen on Feynman’s blackboard); exact context uncertain

text: Everything should be made as simple as possible, but not simpler.
author: Albert Einstein

text: Science is a way of thinking much more than it is a body of knowledge.
author: Carl Sagan
source: Broca’s Brain / popular quote in Sagan’s writings (phrasing varies)

text: Not only is the universe stranger than we imagine, it is stranger than we can imagine.
author: J. B. S. Haldane

text: A scientist is happy, not in resting on his attainments but in the steady acquisition of fresh knowledge.
author: Joseph Priestley

text: The function of imagination in science is to create, out of the known, the unknown.
author: John Tyndall

text: Chance favors the prepared mind.
author: Louis Pasteur
source: Lecture at the University of Lille (1854) (commonly cited)

text: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
author: Aristotle

text: What we know is a drop, what we don’t know is an ocean.
author: Isaac Newton

text: The art and science of asking questions is the source of all knowledge.
author: Thomas Berger

text: Theories should be as simple as possible, but no simpler than that.
author: Albert Einstein

text: For me mathematics is just an instrument I enjoy playing; I don’t care if the problem is important, as long as it’s an interesting puzzle.
author: Freeman Dyson
source: Commonly attributed; I couldn’t confirm a primary source quickly—treat as attribution to verify
